dream: I pressed the turnip down until the stack groaned, then I pressed the wedge on the lid while the air felt thin as a breath. The wide hay lay soft under my hands, a drawing of weight that almost slid. I woke in a tall, dark tree where the card hummed warm at fifty-two. There, the fence stood leaning wrong against a round rock I had never seen. I pressed my weight down on the turnip again, trusting the lean to hold it while the heavy lid felt like a roof I could walk across. The slip chose to move, dragging the dot into a new shape.
